title: Micro Center requires photo ID and signed no-export pledge to buy Nvidia RTX 5090 gaming GPU — buyer forced to sign declaration disclosing install location and promise GPU will remain in the US
key_facts: A customer who bought an RTX 5090 in a PowerSpec AI90 Workstation at Micro Center in Tustin, California had to sign an Advanced Computing Product Purchaser Declaration before the sale, per a Reddit post by u/Krothic.
The form asks for full legal name, address, government photo ID, phone and email, the actual end user, the installation location and the intended use.
It says 'NO EXPORT - NO EXCEPTIONS' and that Micro Center will not sell to anyone who intends to export, resell or transfer the product out of the US.
Micro Center did not say why it began requiring the form; other Reddit commenters said they had not been asked before, and one had signed a similar longer form at Central Computers last summer.
GPUs as powerful as an RTX 4090 or better were first banned for export to China in November 2023; US authorities only recently started clamping down seriously on smuggling.
Three Supermicro employees, including co-founder Yih-Shyan 'Wally' Liaw, are suspected of shipping $2.5 billion of Nvidia hardware to China.
Tom's Hardware says it is unclear how the form will stop smuggling as it does not list the card's serial number; it has asked Micro Center for comment.
quote_evidence: NO EXPORT - NO EXCEPTIONS. Micro Center will not sell this product to a purchaser who intends to export, reexport, resell, transfer, or otherwise cause it to leave the United States, regardless of destination.
It's unclear how these Micro Center forms will stop or prevent the smuggling of RTX 5090 GPUs, especially as they don't list the serial number of the GPU being sold.
why_it_matters_hint: Retail checks on high-end Nvidia graphics cards suggest pressure to stop smuggling to China, but this rests on one customer's post.
event_date: not stated (recent; Tom's Hardware published 2 Oct 2026)
notes: Based on a single customer's Reddit post at one store (Tustin, California); Micro Center has not commented. Wccftech also ran the story on 2 Oct. Whether the policy is chain-wide or required by law is not stated.
